RUGOSA: An extinct tribe of fossil corals, including numerous species, many of them of large size. They are characteristic of the Paleozoic formations. The radiating septs, when present, are usually in multiples of four. See Cyathophylloid.
ROUNCY: A common hackney horse; a nag. [Obs.] he rode upon a rouncy as he could. Chaucer.
RICKRACK: A kind of openwork edging made of serpentine braid.
RUSHBUCKLER: A bullying and violent person; a braggart; a swashbuckler. [Obs.] That flock of stout, bragging rushbucklers. Robynson (More's Utopia).
RESPONSION: 1. The act of answering. [Obs.] 2. (University of Oxford) The first university examination; -- called also little go. See under Little, a.
RAINBOWED: Formed with or like a rainbow.

RAVING: Talking irrationally and wildly; as, a raving lunatic. -- Rav"ing*ly, adv.
RUSTICITY: The quality or state of being rustic; rustic manners; rudeness; simplicity; artlessness. The sweetness and rusticity of a pastoral can not be so well expressed in any other tongue as in the Greek, when rightly mixed and qualified with the Doric dialect. Addison. The Saxons were refined from their rusticity. Sir W. Scott.
ROADSTEAD: An anchorage off shore. Same as Road, 4. Moored in the neighboring roadstead. Longfellow.
RESPIRATOR: A divice of gauze or wire, covering the mouth or nose, to prevent the inhalation of noxious substances, as dust or smoke. Being warmed by the breath, it tempers cold air passing through it, and may also be used for the inhalation of medicated vapors.

RUNDLE: 1. A round; a step of a ladder; a rung. Duppa. 2. A ball. [Obs.] Holland. 3. Something which rotates about an axis, as a wheel, or the drum of a capstan. "An axis or cylinder having a rundle about it." Bp. Wilkins. 4. (Mach.) One of the pins or trundles of a lantern wheel.
REPRINT: 1. To print again; to print a second or a new edition of. 2. To renew the impression of. The whole business of our redemption is . . . to reprint God's image upon the soul. South. A second or a new impression or edition of any printed work; specifically, the publication in one country of a work previously published in another.
RECONTINUANCE: The act or state of recontinuing.
RIVOSE: Marked with sinuate and irregular furrows.
REMINDER: One who, or that which, reminds; that which serves to awaken remembrance.
RONNE: obs. imp. pl., and Ron"nen (, obs. p. p. of Renne, to run. Chaucer.
RAISED: 1. Lifted up; showing above the surroundings; as, raised or embossed metal work. 2. Leavened; made with leaven, or yeast; -- used of bread, cake, etc., as distinguished from that made with cream of tartar, soda, etc. See Raise, v. t., 4. Raised beach. See under Beach, n.

RATIONALISTICAL: Belonging to, or in accordance with, the principles of rationalism. -- Ra`tion*al*is"tic*al*ly, adv.
ROUGHNESS: The quality or state of being rough.
RUSSIAN: Of or pertaining to Russia, its inhabitants, or language. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Russia; the language of Russia. Russian bath. See under Bath.
ROCKLING: Any species of small marine fishes of the genera Onos and Rhinonemus (formerly Motella), allied to the cod. They have three or four barbels.
RADICATED: Rooted; specifically: (a) (Bot.) Having roots, or possessing a well-developed root. (b) (Zoöl.) Having rootlike organs for attachment.
RIGOL: A circle; hence, a diadem. [Obs.] Shak.
RAVELIN: A detached work with two embankments with make a salient angle. It is raised before the curtain on the counterscarp of the place. Formerly called demilune and half-moon.
REEDLESS: Destitute of reeds; as, reedless banks.
REMASTICATE: To chew or masticate again; to chew over and over, as the cud.
RAIAE: The order of elasmobranch fishes which includes the sawfishes, skates, and rays; -- called also Rajæ, and Rajii.
ROPILY: In a ropy manner; in a viscous or glutinous manner.
REPUTABLE: Having, or worthy of, good repute; held in esteem; honorable; praiseworthy; as, a reputable man or character; reputable conduct. RICINELAIDIC: Pertaining to, or designating, an isomeric modification of ricinoleic acid obtained as a white crystalline solid.

RECAPPER: A tool used for applying a fresh percussion cap or primer to a cartridge shell in reloading it.

RUSTINESS: The quality or state of being rusty.
RAMTIL: A tropical African asteraceous shrub (Guizotia abyssinica) cultivated for its seeds (called ramtil, or niger, seeds) which yield a valuable oil used for food and as an illuminant.
RADIATED: 1. Emitted, or sent forth, in rays or direct lines; as, radiated heat. 2. Formed of, or arranged like, rays or radii; having parts or markings diverging, like radii, from a common center or axis; as, a radiated structure; a radiated group of crystals. 3. (Zoöl.) Belonging to the Radiata.
REINSTATE: To place again in possession, or in a former state; to restore to a state from which one had been removed; to instate again; as, to reinstate a king in the possession of the kingdom. For the just we have said already thet some of them were reinstated in their pristine happiness and felicity. Glanvill.
ROUND-BACKED: Having a round back or shoulders; round-shouldered.
RESOURCELESS: Destitute of resources. Burke. -- Re*source"less*ness, n. R. Browning.
ROBORANT: Strengthening. -- n. (Med.) A strengthening medicine; a tonic.
RHINOPLASTY: Plastic surgery of the nose to correct deformity or to replace lost tissue. Tissue may be transplanted from the patient's cheek, forehead, arm, etc., or even from another person.

RESPECTANT: Placed so as to face one another; -- said of animals.

REPOUSSE: (a) Formed in relief, as a pattern on metal. REVOLUTIVE: Inclined to revolve things in the mind; meditative. [Obs.] Feltham.

REVISORY: Having the power or purpose to revise; revising. Story.
RODENTIA: An order of mammals having two (rarely four) large incisor teeth in each jaw, distant from the molar teeth. The rats, squirrels, rabbits, marmots, and beavers belong to this order. RECOVEREE: The person against whom a judgment is obtained in common recovery.

REREFIEF: A fief held of a superior feudatory; a fief held by an under tenant. Blackstone.
ROMANTICNESS: The state or quality of being romantic; widness; fancifulness. Richardson.
REGRETFUL: Full of regret; indulging in regrets; repining. -- Re*gret"ful*ly, adv.
RECENTLY: Newly; lately; freshly; not long since; as, advices recently received.
REJECTITIOUS: Implying or requiring rejection; rejectable. Cudworth.
RETROUSSE: Turned up; -- said of a pug nose.

RIBIBE: 1. A sort of stringed instrument; a rebec. [Obs.] Nares. 2. An old woman; -- in contempt. [Obs.] Chaucer. 3. A bawd; a prostitute. [Obs.] B. Jonson.
RATCH: Same as Rotche. A ratchet wheel, or notched bar, with which a pawl or chick works.
RECOLLECTIVE: Having the power of recollecting. J. Foster.
RECREMENTITIAL: Of the nature of a recrement. See Recrement,2 (b). "Recrementitial fluids." Dunglison.

RETROCOPULATION: Copulation from behind. Sir T. Browne.
REMAND: To recommit; to send back. Remand it to its former place. South. Then were they remanded to the cage again. Bunyan. The act of remanding; the order for recommitment.
REVELOUS: Fond of festivity; given to merrymaking or reveling. [Obs.] Companionable and revelous was she. Chaucer.
ROSTRIFERA: A division of pectinibranchiate gastropods, having the head prolonged into a snout which is not retractile.

REPLICATED: Folded over or backward; folded back upon itself; as, a replicate leaf or petal; a replicate margin of a shell.
